answer: The dyehouse smells of indigo, vats steaming in a row along the wall. Proof of dyer via indigo skein tally — a skein the dyer dips only after 39 skeins hold their dye without one fading at the rinse, each dipped by the dyer himself. mirror stirs the vat and skims the flower off the top. delta dips the skeins in slow and lifts them to oxidise in the air. hollow rinses the skeins in cold water and hangs them to dry. Thirty-nine skeins must hold their dye without one fading at the rinse, and the next still fades where the vat ran weak.
